messages:
deploy-bot: PROD deploy started: rolling canary -> v2.5.3-feature/emb-cache across eu-west1 and us-central1

oncall-ingress: paging — seeing alerts for /v1/embeddings p95 spike and 5xxs, grabbing logs now

sre-liz: confirmed, lots of `redis` connection errors from emb-service canary pods (connection timeout / pool exhausted), p95 ~420ms on canary, baseline ~70ms

eng-oliver: fyi this deploy introduced a cache-key namespace change (namespaced keys -> `emb:v2:{id}`), might be causing cache stampede + many cache misses which hit redis hard

oncall-ingress: trying feature-flag kill switch first: toggling `emb_cache.v2` -> off via console

ops-bot: flag toggle attempt returned 503 from config-service (rate-limited). Toggle did NOT propagate to canaries

oncall-ingress: flag didn't propagate. need manual rollback. Initiating: `kubectl -n inference rollout undo deployment/emb-service --to-revision=5`

deploy-bot: rollback started for emb-service (canary rollout paused -> undo to last stable)

eng-oliver: scaling canary pods down as well to stop new traffic: `kubectl scale deploy/emb-service --replicas=0 -n inference --selector=canary=true`

sre-liz: after rollback + scale-down we see redis errors drop immediately, p95 back to ~78ms in us-central within 90s :white_check_mark:

sre-liz: sample logs during failure for posterity:
```
ERROR redis: i/o timeout connecting to 10.2.3.4:6379
WARN connection pool exhausted (max 50)
TRACE embed_handler: fallback -> direct compute
```

pm-ana: Do we have customer impact? which customers saw errors?

cs-raj: Only two paying tenants showed elevated 5xx in the last 20m (acct-842 and acct-119). Not customer-wide. I've pinged both and opened Triage tickets. They replied, "seeing intermittent failures", not complete outage

oncall-ingress: running smoke checks: `curl -sS https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health` -> `{\"status\":\"ok\"}`. Running an E2E embeddings sample now, response looks good

eng-oliver: root cause hypothesis: cache key rename + no gradual warm-up caused massive cache misses. Config-service 503 prevented kill switch from propagating to canary pool. Fix plan: revert key rename in next PR + add backoff and circuit-breaker on redis client + add preflight cache warm-up for future rollouts. I'll own the PR

pm-ana: please include why config-service returned 503 in the postmortem — that gating failure is concerning

oncall-ingress: creating incident ticket IR-639123 — mitigation complete, assigning postmortem to eng-oliver. Handoff to morning oncall @sre-morning for follow-up and customer comms

sre-morning: acknowledged, will pick this up in the morning and coordinate postmortem

deploy-bot: incident marked mitigated by oncall-ingress at 6391240180

oncall-ingress: quick actionable follow-ups: 1) revert key change + PR by eng-oliver (owner), 2) add flag fallback path when config-service is unreachable (owner: eng-platform), 3) run a replay test to validate cache warm-up (owner: eng-ml). Will add timelines in the incident ticket.

pm-ana: thanks — add customer notes and responsible contacts to IR-639123

cs-raj: I will follow up with both affected customers in the morning with a short incident summary and ETA for a permanent fix

oncall-ingress: closing Slack thread, moving to incident channel ticket. If anything resurfaces ping me directly. :white_check_mark:
